anchor: I have had playmates, I have had companions
note: Companions: people who keep one company.

anchor: my joyful school-days
note: Lamb attended Christ’s Hospital from 1782 to 1789 and there met Coleridge, whose friendship lasted all their lives.

anchor: I have been carousing
note: Carousing: drinking and making merry in a noisy group.

anchor: Drinking late, sitting late
note: Carousing means noisy, hearty drinking with friends.

anchor: with my bosom cronies
note: Cronies: close friends of long standing.

anchor: I loved a Love once, fairest among women
note: Love here is capitalized as a name or title for the woman he loved.

anchor: Closed are her doors on me
note: The woman he loved has shut him out, ending their friendship.

anchor: Like an ingrate, I left my friend
note: Ingrate: an ungrateful person, one who does not give thanks.

anchor: Left him, to muse on the old familiar faces
note: Muse: to think deeply and quietly.

anchor: Ghost-like I paced round the haunts
note: Haunts: places one often visits, like childhood scenes.

anchor: Earth seem’d a desert I was bound to traverse
note: Traverse: to travel across, to pass over.

anchor: Why wert not thou born in my father’s dwelling?
note: Wert: were. He wishes his friend had been born his brother.

anchor: When maidens such as Hester die
note: Maidens: young unmarried women. Hester’s death is named in the first line.

anchor: Their place ye may not well supply
note: Supply: to fill, to take the place of.

anchor: To think upon the wormy bed
note: The grave, where worms feed on the body.

anchor: A springy motion in her gait
note: Gait: a manner of walking.

anchor: A rising step, did indicate
note: Indicate: to show or point to.

anchor: a joy to that allied
note: Allied: closely related, joined. Her joy was near kin to pride.

anchor: She did inherit
note: Inherit: to receive from one’s nature or family.

anchor: Her parents held the Quaker rule
note: Quakers, or the Society of Friends, are a Christian group whose meetings are held in silence. Lamb says their rule “cools the human feeling.”

anchor: Which doth the human feeling cool
note: Lamb says the Quaker rule of plain living cooled natural feeling.

anchor: But she was train’d in Nature’s school
note: Trained by nature, not by her sober family.

anchor: A waking eye, a prying mind
note: Prying: eagerly curious, always looking into things.

anchor: A hawk’s keen sight ye cannot blind
note: Keen: sharp and quick. Hester sees as clearly as a hawk.

anchor: My sprightly neighbour!
note: Sprightly: lively, full of spirit.

anchor: as heretofore
note: Heretofore: before this time, up to now.

anchor: A sweet fore-warning?
note: Fore-warning: a sign given in advance.

anchor: I saw where in the shroud did lurk
note: Lurk: to lie hidden. The baby is hidden in her burial cloth.

anchor: A flow’ret crushed in the bud
note: Flow’ret: a small flower, here one crushed before it opens.

anchor: A nameless piece of Babyhood
note: The baby died before she was named.

anchor: Was in her cradle-coffin lying
note: The coffin is small and cradle-like.

anchor: Extinct, with scarce the sense of dying
note: Extinct: put out, no longer living or burning.

anchor: So soon to exchange the imprisoning womb
note: Womb: the organ where a child grows before birth.

anchor: Through glasses of mortality
note: Mortality: the state of being subject to death. The eye is a glass through which one sees life.

anchor: Riddle of destiny, who can show
note: Destiny: a person’s fixed fate. Lamb asks what her short life was for.

anchor: Shall we say, that Nature blind
note: Lamb wonders if Nature simply stopped, changed her mind, or ran out of strength.

anchor: Or lack’d she the Promethean fire
note: In Greek myth Prometheus stole fire from heaven and gave it to humans. “Promethean fire” here means the power to give life.

anchor: That should thy little limbs have quicken’d
note: Quicken’d: given life to, brought to life.

anchor: Or did the stern-eyed Fate descry
note: Descry: to catch sight of, to see at a distance.

anchor: Thenceforward drags a maimed life?
note: Maimed: crippled, wounded so as to be disabled.

anchor: The economy of Heaven is dark
note: Economy: the way something is ordered or managed. Heaven’s plan is hidden from us.

anchor: More brief than fly ephemeral
note: Ephemeral: lasting a very short time. The mayfly lives for about a day.

anchor: shrivell’d crones
note: Crones: withered old women, who live long while babies die.

anchor: Stiffen with age to stocks and stones
note: Stocks and stones: lifeless things, as the old turn stiff.

anchor: And crabbed use the conscience sears
note: Crabbed: cross and bitter. Sears: burns, makes hard and unfeeling.

anchor: Mother’s prattle, mother’s kiss
note: Prattle: simple, childish talk, baby chatter.

anchor: See them laid upon the hearse
note: Hearse: a vehicle that carries a coffin to the grave.

anchor: Pictured trophies to their grave
note: Trophies: carvings or emblems placed on a monument.

anchor: And we, churls, to thee deny
note: Churls: rude, low-born men, common people.
